narration_pass_directives:
This review is narrated in English for an English-speaking audience. Write caption_ko as the English on-screen caption - the field keeps its name for schema compatibility, but the text must be English, not Korean. tts_en carries the same sentence for the voice, and the two may be identical. Do not write Korean anywhere in this script.

Do NOT prune narration to a handful of lines. The edit plan already decided where narration goes and reserved a block for each candidate, measured against a reference review of this same film that narrates over 41.9 percent of its runtime. Removing a candidate leaves that block as silent film footage and breaks the 40 percent floor the project approved. Use narration on at least 85 percent of candidates. Reserve use_narration=false for the few beats where a line of the film's own dialogue lands in the same seconds and would be talked over.

The film's own narrator speaks in several of these clips. Do not repeat what he says - add the causal link, the stake, or the reading of a character that he leaves implicit.

Sentences run 8 to 14 words. Vary how they open; do not begin consecutive lines the same way. Write in plain, concrete American English - no reviewer cliches, no 'masterfully', no rhetorical questions beyond the two allowed.

The review stops before the outcome of the final confrontation. Nothing may state or imply who fires first, who lives, or what is found afterwards.
